Q: Ai Neural Network | C++ | Project Guidance --- Matrix Part A:

Tactical note: vector of vectors syntax is simple to use, but at runtime it can be surprisingly slow. Each vector is typically a pointer to a dynamically allocated array of data and a couple bookkeeping variables. The outer vector is a pointer to an array of vectors that each point to an array of data, and none of these arrays are likely anywhere near the others in memory, preventing the CPU from making the best, or even good, use of its cache. Reading from cache is fast. Reading from RAM, is an order or two magnitudes slower. Anytime you have to leave the CPU to get something, you'll be spending more time than you likely do processing it.

This is particularly noticeable in small matrices where the CPU loads the array of vectors into cache, does some quick math to find the first data array it needs and then has to stop and wait as it loads the first data array. Then a bit of math and then it has to go looking for and load the second data array. And then a bit more math and then waiting on the third array...

But with if all the data was contiguous in storage, the CPU can read and possibly cache the entire small matrix in one shot, or at least start pre-loading the cache while you're computing what's already in the cache because there is no doubt. It just picks up where it left off.

Replace std::vector<std::vector<T>> data; with something like what doug describes here and you may see huge performance increases with very little effort. You can also perform the arithmetic yourself and get rid of the pointers via striding.

Or just use Eigen as recommended because it's already doing these tricks and many more. Nice to know where the sneaky stuff Eigen's doing for you came from, though.

Q: SpringBoot unit test does not use @EnableAutoConfiguration annotation from Application class A:

I'm had this issue with version 2.0.9.RELEASE, which I have to use to stay in compliance with my company standards. What worked for me was:

@SpringBootTest(properties="spring.autoconfigure.exclude=org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.jdbc.DataSourceAutoConfiguration")

I can't say for certain if this is an issue with @EnableAutoConfiguration in my version of Springboot, but with version 2.1.5.RELEASE, I do not have to set the property with the @SpringBootTest to make this work.

Q: Is it possible to implement a CSS class in crystal reports for Visual Studio 2012 (winform or WPF application)? A:

Yes. you can do this.

1.Right-click in the embedded Crystal Reports Designer and select Set CSS Class.
2.In the Object Scope field, select the objects or sections you would like the class to be applied to.
3.Enter the name of the class in the CSS Class Name field.

Tip Use CssClass in the Properties window to view, edit, or delete the class values for a specific report object or section.

4.Click OK.
5.Save the report.
6.Access the .aspx file in your project.
7.In the HTML tab of the .aspx file, reference an external style sheet that has the class already defined, or enter the class value.

For example:

<HTML>
    <STYLE>
        .classname
        {
            background-color:808080; border-color:000000; color:000000; font-family:Arial; font-weight:bold; font-style:italic; }
   <STYLE>
</HTML>

Source: SAP Help Portal

I Hope it will help you.

Q: Transcript file from MS Teams A:

You can get Teams meeting transcripts with speaker names via webhook, but you’d need to use the Microsoft Graph API. The transcript content will be returned as a .vtt stream with speaker names and timestamps.

There are a few restrictions with this method, namely that the host needs to join the meeting and you need to explicitly start the transcription each time.

To get around these, it may be easier to consider other ways of getting transcripts from microsoft teams (desktop recording, meeting bots, etc)
